method: independent approval pass (separate from the authoring pass): re-verified excerpt bytes and sha256 (90ec964e...eca19) of book_667380 against Novgorod-game-base books-evidence-v1/history-events-knowledge.csv rows book_id 667380 para_no 486 and 487 (each quote one sentence, byte-exact); recomputed formal_range and formal_game_timestamp_range against owner decisions D19 and D22 and the novgorod_julian_lmst_1230_1233_v2 epoch (Julian common years 1230 and 1231; 256*1440=368640; 730*1440=1051200); checked that source_precision and range_semantics state a day-exact start and a year-level end without overclaiming; checked that no price, population, inventory or mortality magnitude is inferred; checked prior-decision snapshot sha256 equals the previously approved decision bytes; checked the diff touches only this family's files.
rationale: Reissues the record to add source book_667380 (¶486 frost on Воздвижение 1230-09-14; ¶487 arrival of German bread during 1231) and to narrow the formal range accordingly: start_inclusive moves from calendar-year precision (1230-01-01) to calendar-day precision (1230-09-14, owner decision D19); end_exclusive moves from 1231-01-01 to 1232-01-01 at year precision, reflecting the source's year-level dating of the famine's continuation through 1231 and its cessation (owner decision D22). The record still keeps numerical magnitudes unauthored and preserves hidden-phase/knowledge separation.
limitations: The end boundary (1232-01-01) is authored at year precision, not day precision: ¶487 dates the German bread's arrival, and hence the famine's practical cessation, only to source year 1231 without an exact month or day. The start boundary (1230-09-14) is day-exact per ¶486. Local effect magnitudes remain separate approved-profile dependencies rather than hidden defaults.
